newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end at day lows on futures-selling.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end at day lows on futures-selling.

text.p: South African shares dipped as a late wave of futures-related selling hit the index and caused it to finish at its day lows, dealers said.
Futures traders took advantage of a wary market to dump stock and drive the index down in the hope of buying back at lower levels.
"There was a lot of futures-related selling at the end," one dealer said.
After the rand-led fall last week all market eyes were nervously fixed on the performance of the ailing currency and the bonds market.
There was no repeat of last week's dramatic swings, but the share market was still nervous enough to lock into a downward path early on.
The all-share index ended dropped 18.5 points to end at 6,952.9 as industrials fell 18.8 points to 8,175.3.
Golds did better as shares firmed on a steadier bullion price, though it is still below the important $380 an ounce level. The golds index ended up 9.9 points at 1,732.4.
